title: Ending without chasing former excitement

captions.physics: Stopping a leisure form without pleasure
captions.emotions: Experiencing a changing response to transition

meaning: Freedom to experience change supports leisure together when wanting earlier excitement back leaves a completed form free from compulsory repetition.
text: A completed habit can still hold the promise of a former feeling. Death in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes stopping a leisure form that stopped delighting. The Devil in energy leans towards recovering earlier enjoyment. The Wheel of Fortune in emotions makes responses changeable: relief appears beside wanting another attempt at the old activity. These fluctuations require no instant reversal. Both may hear today’s wishes without turning remembered excitement into the compulsory direction of every following free evening.

For example, you end regular sessions of one competitive game. A new walk feels pleasant and calm, but recalling an earlier victory invites playing again to recover its mood. **A good memory creates no duty to restore the old script.** You can share the recollection and continue the chosen outing. Changing feeling remains permissible without proving new leisure inferior or requiring both to resume everything completed to preserve togetherness and former enthusiasm.

The difficulty is answering every dip by returning to a familiar promise. You repeat, await excitement and become disappointed when it differs from memory. An ending becomes repeated attempts to recover the past. Freedom helps when allowing fluctuation without acting on the first impulse. Both can acknowledge a wish to return and still choose present enjoyment, preserving earlier experience’s value without immediately reproducing it.
